key_insight: A quantum generator can train only a linear output layer, with the tested entangling reservoirs offering no systematic advantage over a reservoir with no gates.
engineering_relevance: Fixed quantum circuits avoid circuit-training barren plateaus, while competitive gate-free reservoirs suggest opportunities to reduce quantum hardware demands.
method: Encode random latent vectors into quantum states, apply a fixed unitary, and measure features for a trainable linear output layer.
Use Pauli propagation to analyze how Clifford circuits and added T gates transform encoding-defined functions.
Compare Clifford, T-doped, Haar-random brickwork, and gate-free reservoirs.
evidence_signal: Tests on one- and two-dimensional distributions, using expectation values and single measurements, found no systematic improvement from Clifford-generated entanglement or Haar-random reservoir nonstabilizerness.
watch_item: The findings are specific to the proposed encoding and tested low-dimensional distributions; broader generative advantages remain unestablished.
